A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NEURONAL research work. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original pruning experiments measuring perplexity and zero-shot accuracy, alongside component and calibration ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 reports original pruning evaluations, revised benchmark results, and calibration analyses. These qualify independently of the competitor runtimes attributed to earlier papers.

M1.justification: The block-wise followed by row-wise sparsity allocation, alignment criterion, mask updates, and adaptive parameter search remain unchanged in Equations 1–2 and Algorithm 1. The block-only adaptation for SparseGPT also remains. Revised selected parameters and scores do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use WikiText2, C4, PTB, and the same seven zero-shot tasks: RTE, WinoGrande, BoolQ, HellaSwag, ARC-e, ARC-c, and OBQA. Additional sparsity levels and runtime measurements change experimental settings, without adding datasets or task requirements.

E2.justification: V2 adds AlphaPruning throughout the Magnitude, MULTIFLOW, and Wanda benchmark comparisons. BESA and DSA enter the limited runtime/perplexity comparison in Table 7, with their runtimes attributed to prior papers. Conversely, the Magnitude-based 13B comparisons at 70% and 80% sparsity disappear from v1 Table 3 to v2 Table 6; the 60% comparison remains.

E3.justification: V2 Table 7 introduces sparsity-allocation runtime measurements and 65%/75% sparsity evaluations for LLaMA-1 7B with Wanda. Figure 2 adds an AlphaPruning parameter sweep, while the retained OWL and schedule studies narrow from Wanda plus MULTIFLOW to Wanda. The main calibration sizes, sequence length, model inventory, and hardware setup remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 removes the experiments isolating the block and row components in v1 Tables 4 and 17–18. It also removes the OWL sensitivity results on C4/PTB in v1 Figures 5–8 and the MULTIFLOW sensitivity branch, while adding AlphaPruning sensitivity in Figure 2. NEURONAL parameter-selection and calibration-size/seed analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report calibration experiments using seeds 0, 16, and 46 with mean and standard deviation at 60%, 70%, and 80% sparsity. V1 Tables 5, 19–20 correspond to v2 Tables 8, 21–22. No new uncertainty-reporting or significance-testing practice appears.

E6.justification: Many NEURONAL results change alongside new AlphaPruning and runtime entries. For example, 70% Wanda/Phi-2.7B WikiText2 perplexity changes from 89.9 to 88.3 (v1 Table 1; v2 Table 3). The 80% Wanda/LLaMA-1 13B result changes from 64.0 to 156.4 (v1 Table 3; v2 Table 6), with selected parameters also revised. These are reported result revisions, not established algorithmic improvements. Component-ablation and some 13B results disappear; SparseGPT scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The pruning-mask and normalized activation-alignment definitions remain mathematically unchanged. Neither version supplies substantive theorems or proofs. V2 removes an explanatory comparison with the standard reconstruction-error objective, without changing the proposed mathematical framework.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains adaptive, gradient-free block/row pruning. V2 adds an explicit performance-runtime trade-off claim in the abstract and conclusion and qualifies performance superiority as occurring in most cases, refining v1's broader outperformance wording.

C2.justification: V2 adds a substantive argument that dense-only importance metrics overlook how pruning changes downstream block importance. It removes v1's component-level interpretation attributing most gains to block allocation and increasing benefits at high sparsity to row allocation. Runtime becomes a central competitive advantage, and the known extra-forward-pass overhead leaves the limitations list, although it remains documented. OPT sensitivity and SparseGPT restrictions are retained.

D1.justification: V2 explicitly documents baseline settings OWL M=5 and λ=0.08 and AlphaPruning ε=0.3, adds quantitative runtime information, and revises selected block/row parameters in appendix Tables 23–24. Dataset descriptions and size information are shortened. The code-access statement, calibration construction, candidate parameter sets, and A100 hardware disclosure remain.

R1.justification: Positioning expands from an OWL-centered critique to comparisons across hyperparameter dependence, runtime, and dense/sparse information use. V2 adds AlphaPruning, DSA, and Shortened LLaMA citations and substantially expands discussion of BESA. It removes the Dodge et al. corpus-documentation citation. The main change is the broader competitive framing, beyond citation additions.

P1.justification: V2 replaces the observational-study narrative with a three-part limitations discussion, moves schedule justification into Section 4.3, compresses dataset descriptions, rewrites the abstract and conclusion, and reorganizes the appendices. These are substantial narrative and structural revisions.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column layout, adds a front-page runtime plot and comparison tables, and consolidates the hyperparameter plots. V1 Figure 1 becomes a Wanda-only schedule table. Detailed zero-shot results move to the appendix while summary tables enter the main text. Several ablation displays disappear, and retained plots are resized and relocated.

improvement.justification: The added AlphaPruning comparisons and runtime analysis address important gaps in v1, but removing the component ablations weakens support for the two-stage design. The new runtime argument also overstates its evidence: Table 7's approximately 43,000 versus 237.1 seconds implies about 181-fold, while the text claims four orders of magnitude. Tables 3 and 7 additionally disagree on the apparently matching 70% Wanda perplexity, reporting 21.5 and 20.7. These material benefits and harms leave the net quality direction unclear.
